items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: I was roommates with a painter named Bob Thompson who is getting some attention right now

ctx.x: Well in New York I knew a lot of jazz musicians and I knew them very well. I mean that was a part of our world. The thing about the lower Manhattan arts scene in the 1960s was about as close as America ever got to say Montmartre at the turn of the 19th and 20th century, the modernism there. A great concentration of artists of all disciplines living in a relatively small area. They all knew each other, they all hung out together, they went to each other’s parties, they drank together, and the exchange was…

think was one of Ornette’s greatest, greatest tunes. You’d go by, I was roommates with a painter named Bob Thompson who is getting some attention right now, and Bob, he’s been dead for several years. And he’d be there working and he’d be there working and have his music on. That’s one, painters could listen to jazz and work. I always envied that. They’d have it up really, really loud and he’d be practically dancing into his canvas and he’d be talking about it. And it’s the same with all the musicians, I mean…

Did you ever have an occasion where you wrote about a musician and made some opinions of your own, perhaps some assumptions, and then heard from that musician saying, “I was not thinking that” or “that was not my intention?”
